messages:
Ravi: FYI we're moving away from org-wide long-lived automation tokens (PATs/service-accounts) towards short-lived Vault-issued credentials (dynamic roles). This affects CI, infra provisioning scripts, and a bunch of automation. Opt-in pilot: Aug 1. Enforcement (deny token use for automation): Sept 30. Docs: https://go/redwood/vault-dynamic-auth :lock:

Nia: Is this only for GitHub Actions/workflows or broader?

Ravi: Broader. CI is the first priority because it's high-risk, but any automation that uses static tokens needs a plan. We'll publish per-system guides (CI, Terraform, k8s controllers, monitoring hooks).

Caro: How will this work for self-hosted/on-prem environments with no Vault access?

Ravi: Two paths: 1) For on-prem with network access, we recommend deploying the lightweight Vault Agent sidecar or using AppRole with short TTLs. 2) For air-gapped installs, we'll provide a signed JWT bridge and a documented HSM/KMS workflow. Details in the private-deploy section of the migration guide.

Diego: Who's building the migration tooling? Replacing secrets across hundreds of repos is a pain.

Ravi: Diego/infra team will ship an automated replacer (repo-scanner + PR generator) that can insert Vault lookups like:

```
- name: Fetch credentials
  run: |
    export DB_PASSWORD=$(vault kv get -field=password secret/ci/db-prod)
```

Plus a local test harness and feature-flagged compatibility layer for gradual rollout. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-infra/ci-vault-migration

infra-bot: Repo scan scheduled: 2024-08-05 02:00 UTC. Will generate a report and open issues for repos using detected long-lived tokens.

Nia: Anything that will auto-rotate secrets now? I have automation that expects a static token to live for months.

Ravi: We will not silently rotate all tokens. The plan: scan -> notify maintainers -> open migration PRs with a compatibility shim. We will expire tokens for org-level service accounts on Sept 30 unless an exception is approved.

Caro: Exceptions? What criteria?

Ravi: Exceptions are allowed for vendors that can't support dynamic creds, or for legacy systems that require a phased migration. They require an Eng-Security review, compensating controls (IP allowlist, auditing), and a max 90-day extension. Submit via https://go/redwood/eng-security-requests tag "dynamic-auth-exception".

Diego: Will this impact Dedicated/Private customers' managed runners or infra we operate for them?

Ravi: For managed Dedicated: we'll migrate creds on behalf of customers and coordinate maintenance windows. For customer-managed Private installs: we'll provide the integration docs and an operator checklist; we won't enforce on their infrastructure unless contractually agreed.

Nia: Does this change our Terraform state/auth patterns? We still have a few CI jobs that apply infra with a token.

Ravi: Yes — Terraform runs should adopt Vault agent/short-lived tokens. We're working with Platform to publish a Terraform-runner pattern that fetches ephemeral creds. There's a migration section with examples.

eng-security-bot: Policy update v1 published: https://go/redwood/policies/dynamic-automation-credentials (effective 2024-09-30).

Caro: Rollout support? Can infra team pair with squads to help the first 10 repos?

Diego: We can do office hours + pairings. I'll schedule two sessions next week: Wed/Thu 1400 UTC.

Ravi: Owners: Diego/infra -> migration tooling + PRs. Nia -> docs + FAQ + comms. Eng-Security -> policy enforcement + exceptions. Contact: #eng-security and #eng-infra.

Nia: I'll draft the announcement email and a short migration checklist. Will link automated scan report and help signup sheet.

Ravi: TL;DR: Replace long-lived automation tokens with Vault dynamic credentials. Pilot Aug 1, enforcement Sept 30. Scan and PR tooling live, migration repo + docs: https://go/redwood/vault-dynamic-auth. Ping us with repo links or questions.
